worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,-y\le x\le 2y}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}x{e}^{{y}^{3}}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{2y}x{e}^{{y}^{3}}\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{2y}x{e}^{{y}^{3}}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{3}}[{\int }_{-y}^{2y}x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{3}}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{-y}^{2y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{3}}(2{y}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2})dy \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{y}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{3}}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{y}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{3}}\,dy & =\frac{1}{2}{[{e}^{{y}^{3}}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{8}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{8}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
